claim.why_it_matters: Both normative constants in 15.27.3 (E function returned value rules 1 and 3) carry an embedded ZERO WIDTH SPACE (U+200B) inside the digit string, at the point where the PDF line was re-flowed. The character is invisible when rendered, so a human reading the markdown sees the correct value, but any mechanical use of the transcription -- grep for the constant, copy/paste into a test golden, or a script parsing the literal -- gets a string that is not a number and will not match. These are the only two U+200B characters in the entire transcription, so this is a localized artifact and not a transcription convention. Digit counts were verified against the rendered page: rule 1 = 31 digits after the point, rule 3 = 33 digits after the point; both match the PDF exactly once the U+200B is removed.

verdict.reasoning: CONFIRMED by independent inspection of both sources. (1) PDF: rendered page 873 at 300 dpi (printed folio 843) and cropped/upscaled both constant lines of 15.27.3. The printed glyphs read, unambiguously and unbroken on a single centered line each: rule 1 '(2 + 0.7182818284590452353602874713526).' and rule 3 '(2.718281828459045235360287471352662).' There is no hyphen, no line break, no visible gap, and no extra spacing anywhere inside either digit run. (2) Markdown: checked specs/ISO_COBOL.md directly (not just the extracted work-unit slice, ruling out a pipeline artifact of page_workunit.py) -- both literals contain a U+200B, at 'ISO_COBOL.md' offsets inside '...28747135<U+200B>26)' and '...4713<U+200B>52662)'. (3) The claim quotes both sources accurately, character for character. (4) Removing the two U+200B yields exactly the PDF strings: 31 decimals for rule 1, 33 decimals for rule 3, both confirmed programmatically and by glyph-by-glyph reading of the render. (5) A full-file scan for Cf/Cc/zero-width/NBSP/soft-hyphen characters returns exactly two hits in the whole transcription, both of them these U+200B -- so this is a localized artifact, not a transcription convention. Refutation angles all fail: nothing is missing or reflowed onto an adjacent line; this is not page-break furniture, markdown line wrapping, or hyphenation (a wrap would be normalizable whitespace, whereas a zero-width character sits inside a normative numeric literal and survives whitespace normalization); and it does change meaning for any mechanical consumer -- the transcribed literal is not a parseable number and will not grep-match or copy/paste into a golden. Severity 'cosmetic' is right for a human reader, but the defect is real.
verdict.corrected_description: Finding is real; one detail of the stated rationale is wrong. The PDF does NOT re-flow either line -- both constants are printed unbroken on a single centered line, so the U+200B does not mark a PDF line break. Its origin is the extraction pipeline (a text-run boundary inside the PDF content stream, invisible in the rendering), which makes it a pure transcription artifact with no counterpart in the printed page. Also stronger than claimed: these two U+200B are not merely the only two U+200B, they are the only invisible/format-category characters (Cf/Cc, zero-width, NBSP, soft hyphen) in the entire transcription. Corrected statement: specs/ISO_COBOL.md page 873, 15.27.3 E function returned value rules 1 and 3, each embed a spurious ZERO WIDTH SPACE (U+200B) inside a normative decimal literal -- '0.71828182845904523536028747135<U+200B>26' and '2.7182818284590452353602874713<U+200B>52662'. The PDF prints '(2 + 0.7182818284590452353602874713526).' (31 decimals) and '(2.718281828459045235360287471352662).' (33 decimals), unbroken. Fix: delete both U+200B; the resulting digit strings then match the PDF exactly.
